signals.text: A standing order repays a private loan to Andrea Widmer.
On average 250.82 was left per month over the last 6 months; in 3 months more went out than came in (2026-05, 2026-06, 2026-10).
Sparkonto holds 4'919.20, 49 % of its goal "Notgroschen CHF 10'000".
Steuerverwaltung des Kantons Bern is due on 30.11.2026: 1'180.00, "Steuern 2026, 3. Rate (provisorisch)".
Paid into pillar 3a in 2026: 3'300.00 of the maximum 7'258.00; after the standing orders 3'658.00 is missing.
6 payments of together 3'155.45 are due in the next 30 days.
Regular payments that cost more within a year: KPT Krankenkasse AG from 296.80 to 399.40 on 24.12.2025.
On 23.12.2026, the day before the next salary, 5'363.93 is left on Privatkonto after 6 payments, 198.66 a day. A month's spending is about 5'395.90.
Spending averaged 5'511.93 a month over the last 6 months, highest in 2026-06.
6 payments of together 3'155.45 leave before the salary on 24.12.2026.
The 6 largest monthly payments add up to 2'103.25 a month.

hero_question.reason: The hero shows what is left at month's end (CHF 250.82 on average, with three negative months), which directly answers Jana's stated complaint that far less remains at the end of the month than she expected now that she earns well.

about_customer.reason: Every tile maps to a specific fact of Jana's life: her monthly leftover, the CHF 150 repayment to her mother Andrea Widmer, the emergency fund she asks about, the provisional tax bill from her first tax year, the pillar 3a she opened in 2026, and her upcoming rent, insurance and tax payments.

titles.reason: All titles are short, concrete and read like a person wrote them ('Provisional tax bill', 'Emergency fund', 'What is left at month's end' echoing her own words), and each matches what its tile shows.

not_empty_or_repeated.reason: No tile is empty or zero, and the single tax-bill detail standing beside the due-soon list that contains it is the sanctioned detail-beside-the-list pattern rather than a repeat.

coherent.reason: Under the name 'Every month' the board tells one story Jana would follow: what survives the month, what she must pay (parents, tax, bills) and what she is building (emergency fund, pillar 3a), answering both halves of her question about what she can afford and how to build something up.
